# The multi-window restore seams have no implementer, so a saved topology can never be reloaded

## Context

The operator's stated prio-zero for dock layouts is: *save the layout, reload the multi-window app with the saved layout, get the same multi-window setup back* — and *"i am 99% sure this is not the case."*

He is right, and the reason is not a missing feature. **Every piece is built.** The gap is that nothing implements the two seams that connect them, so the whole path is unreachable from any component.

## Measured at `dev@274b63beac`

The engine ships a complete multi-window save/restore chain:

| piece | file | state |
|---|---|---|
| capture N documents as one v2 record | `model/Persistence.mjs:133` `captureTopologyPerspective()` | built, unit-tested |
| shape-only topology term | `model/Persistence.mjs` `windowFingerprint` | built, validated (never ids or coordinates) |
| slot-indexed restore reconciliation | `model/TopologyReconciler.mjs` (712 lines) | built, unit-tested, fails the ENTIRE restore closed on any invalid slot |
| plan toward a captured layout | `persistence/RestorePlanner.mjs` | built |
| the routing that drives all of it | `ai/client/DockService.mjs:184, :379` | built |

`DockService` reaches a live app through exactly two holder seams — `getDockTopologyDocuments()` (ordered committed documents, primary first) and `commitDockTopologyDocuments()`.

**Neither has an implementation anywhere.**

```
$ grep -rnE "^\s+(async )?getDockTopologyDocuments\s*\(" src/ apps/ examples/ test/ --include="*.mjs"
(none)

$ grep -rnE "^\s+(async )?commitDockTopologyDocuments\s*\(" src/ apps/ examples/ test/ --include="*.mjs"
test/playwright/unit/ai/client/DockService.spec.mjs:544
test/playwright/unit/ai/client/DockService.spec.mjs:631
```

Both definitions are **stub objects inside `DockService`'s own unit spec**. Every reference in the repo lives in exactly two files: the service that requires them (9 hits) and the spec that stubs them (9 hits). `dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs` implements neither; `apps/workstation` implements neither.

So the multi-window restore path is green, validated, and has been exercised only against test doubles. `DockService:171` even handles the absence gracefully — it reports that the component "exposes no `getDockTopologyDocuments()` seam" — which is why this has never surfaced as an error.

## Why this is structural, not one missing method

This is the second instance of one shape found tonight. On #18233 the finding was that `interaction/Preview` and `interaction/DragAffordances` each describe themselves as *"the app-neutral piece every docking workspace composes"* and **no engine workspace composes either**. This is the same defect in the persistence tier: the engine builds the machinery, documents the seam, tests it against stubs, and assembles nothing.

The pattern matters more than either instance. A capability can be fully implemented, fully covered, and still deliver nothing, because coverage against a stub proves the machinery and never the reach. Whatever the fix here, the epic should treat *"is there an implementer, or only a requirer?"* as a standing question.

## Landing-site constraint

There is a standing operator directive on `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs` — *stop adding to this layer* (PR #18213, recorded in its closure comment; see #18208). Adding two methods there is the idiomatic-looking choice and is what the directive forbids.

`window/WorkspaceSet.mjs` already holds what the read seam needs: `ids()`, `getDocument(workspaceId)`, and `adoptTransfer()` for the write half. Whether the seams are answered from the set, from a thin binding, or elsewhere is the implementing PR's decision — but it needs to be made deliberately, and `dock/Workspace.mjs` is not it.

## Acceptance Criteria

> **RESTATED 2026-09-04 after cross-lab review of PR #18253 (@neo-gpt-emmy).** Two ACs were unachievable as written and one was measuring the wrong thing. Both restatements are narrowing, not weakening — each names what it was protecting and what now witnesses it.

- [ ] **AC-1 — RESTATED. The MODEL half closes here; the VIEW half moves to #18272.** A dock host captures a multi-window topology and an N-slot commit restores **every slot's document** atomically — all or none. Witnessed, not inferred.
  - ⚠️ **What this ticket can no longer claim:** that the restored composition is *visible* in the second window. `TopologySeams` converges the primary projection only, and that is structural: **all seven `workspaceSet.register` sites in the repository supply plain-assignment writers**, `dockModel` is not a reactive config, and a vessel's `targetState.document` is written in five places and read only by its own `getDocument`. There is no sibling projection to trigger. Building one is the popup/document-ownership question live on **D#18224**, so it is owned by **#18272** rather than decided here by implementation accident.
  - The original wording ("restore it after a reload, with the same composition") reads as an operator-visible outcome. It was never achievable from a seams PR, and closing #18252 on it would have recorded a screen-level guarantee the code does not make.
- [ ] **AC-2 — RESTATED. Measure concern growth, not line count.** The seams' implementation lives outside `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs` (`window/TopologySeams.mjs`, 105 lines), and `Workspace.mjs` gains **only the composition cost** — one import plus one mixin config, 7 lines, owning no state, no methods and no configs for the concern.
  - The original "line count unchanged" forbids the very vehicle the architecture review endorsed: a mixin cannot be composed without a composition line. It was protecting against the god object absorbing another concern, and 7 lines of composition against 105 lines of concern placed elsewhere is that protection satisfied, not evaded. Graded by the **Stage-0-gated Ownership test** (D#18150): `TopologySeams` owns no state or lifecycle, so it is judged as a protocol surface — minimal, mandatory, resolved by a named external consumer.
- [x] AC-3 — Restore does not replay history. The captured record is a composition state and is applied as one, per the operator's *"reloading an app must not walk through the entire history."*
- [x] AC-4 — A host that implements neither seam behaves exactly as today. Verified: `DockService.restoreTopologyPerspective` filters for missing seams and returns a structured `refusal(...)`; nothing throws. The capability is additive.
- [ ] **AC-5 — RESTATED to follow AC-1.** Mutation-verified: removing the implementation reds the **N-slot atomicity** arm. A green arm over a capability that resolves to a stub is the exact failure this ticket documents — and that bar now applies to the model half, with the view half's mutation bar carried by #18272.
- [x] AC-6 — The `windowFingerprint` stays shape-only. No window ids, no coordinates — ADR 0029's rule. Verified: `model/Persistence.mjs:72` validates it as a JSON record and nothing in the restore path reads geometry.

## Contract Ledger

Backfilled 2026-09-04 (@neo-gpt-emmy, RA-2). Three methods enter a contract with this ticket; a future consumer or reviewer detects drift against this table rather than against the diff.

| method | direction | contract |
|---|---|---|
| `getDockTopologyDocuments()` | **exposed** — resolved by `DockService` | Returns the ordered live committed documents, primary first. A set-less workspace returns `[dockModel]`; an empty set returns `[]`. The read seam that topology CAPTURE and topology RESTORE share, so both see one ordering. |
| `commitDockTopologyDocuments(documents)` | **exposed** — resolved by `DockService` | Atomic multi-document write: every registered slot adopts or none does. Returns `{errors}`; empty means committed. **Returns a refusal rather than throwing** — `restoreTopologyPerspective` branches on `commit?.errors?.length` and does not wrap the call, so a throw escapes the refusal shape as an RPC crash. **Converges the primary projection only** (see AC-1 / #18272). |
| `workspaceSet.adoptAll(documents)` | **consumed** — from `window/WorkspaceSet.mjs` | Slot-ordered, both-or-neither, with two-sided compensation on a writer failure. Refuses on slot-count mismatch, a null slot, or a read-only workspace. Absence is a valid state: a single-document workspace has no set, and `commitDockTopologyDocuments` falls back to the one-document path rather than treating it as an error. |

## Non-goals

- **Pixel geometry as durable state.** Whether window position/size should persist is D#18224's open question to the operator and is not settled here. This ticket restores *composition* — which windows exist and what is in them.
- **Undo/redo across windows.** The transaction/history half of the operator's ask is a separate axis; this one is the reload path, which explicitly must not replay history.
- Changing `TopologyReconciler`, `RestorePlanner` or the capture format. They are built and tested; this is about reaching them.

## Decision Record impact

`aligned-with ADR 0029` — the docking design record. No new docking concept; this connects seams the record already defines.
